summary: City of Hope — one of the nation's premier cancer research and treatment centers — sits right in the middle of Duarte, making this small San Gabriel Valley city of roughly 24,000 an unlikely global healthcare hub wedged against the steep southern face of the San Gabriel Mountains. That proximity to real mountains isn't decorative: the Duarte Bike Trail runs east–west through town, and trailheads into the Angeles National Forest are minutes away, offering genuine ridge-line hiking rather than manicured park loops. With an average daily high of 75°F and nearly 9.5 hours of sunshine year-round, the climate rewards time outdoors almost every day. Financially, the picture is tighter than first impressions suggest — a median home price of $710,700 against a median household income of roughly $98,000 yields a price-to-income ratio above 7:1, well past conventional affordability thresholds, while median rent at nearly $2,000 a month absorbs a meaningful share of pre-tax earnings. The Gold Line light-rail station connects Duarte to Pasadena and downtown Los Angeles, which matters because this is largely a bedroom community despite City of Hope's presence; switching employers locally means limited options. Duarte is a place where mountain access and regional medical prestige coexist with a commuter reality and housing math that demands careful budgeting.
